clue.text: One of perhaps a hundred traitors, said the sansculotte?

definitions.text: One of perhaps a hundred traitors, said the sansculotte?

blocks.clueFragment: One of perhaps a hundred traitors
blocks.note: surface reading: a member of some large band of turncoats
setter's reading: to a French Revolutionary radical, every noble was a traitor to the people

explanation.surface: A ragged revolutionary denounces a crowd of traitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Sansculottes were the working-class radicals of the French Revolution, who sent nobles to the guillotine as enemies of the people.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled noble was exactly what a Revolutionary radical branded an enemy of the nation.

clue.text: One that's fallen for a flat foot

definitions.text: One that's fallen for a flat foot

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who has tumbled, or been taken in, perhaps by a policeman (a flatfoot)
setter's reading: the curved part of the sole has collapsed, which is what produces flat feet

explanation.surface: Someone has fallen for a plodding policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat foot' suggests the slang for a police officer and 'fallen for' suggests romance; medically, flat feet come from a fallen instep.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat feet are caused by a collapsed instep curve, known in everyday speech as fallen arches.

clue.text: Not working, I, with old age creeping up

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving up the column means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
eld is an archaic word for old age

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are retired now that old age is catching up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idle is unoccupied, without employment or activity, so the word describes a person off duty.

clue.text: Organized 10 in an annuity scheme - how melodramatic!

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the middle of the scheme, so one word is placed within another

blocks.note: a tontine is a shared annuity where the last survivors take everything
ran a business means organized it
10 across is ODDS, and SP (starting price) is the betting odds at the off

explanation.surface: A financial adviser arranges odds within a pension scheme, with theatrical flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: Transpontine literally means 'across the bridge', after the lurid melodramas staged at theatres on the south bank of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey-side London theatres were famed for sensational plays, so the adjective came to mean overwrought and theatrical.

clue.text: The best thing_for weightwatchers to avoid?

blocks.note: first meaning: the finest part, as in the pick of the crop
second meaning: the rich fatty dairy product dieters steer clear of

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as advice about what dieters should skip; the two parts are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the cream of society' means the elite, while the dairy topping is notoriously fattening.

clue.text: "But falls into-and low price" (T Night)

blocks.note: surface reading: a quotation with a word missing after 'into'
setter's reading: the line is Orsino's in Twelfth Night, speaking of how love's value drops 'even in a minute'

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare about something losing its value, with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Orsino says anything love takes in 'falls into abatement and low price'. T Night is short for Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing noun means a lessening or reduction, matching the companion phrase about a fall in worth.

clue.text: Four-inch bananas

definitions.note: the clue gives a measure; the answer is the unit of that size
a plural fruit; the answer is the bunch they grow in

blocks.note: first meaning: the unit used to measure a horse's height, equal to four inches
second meaning: a cluster of bananas growing together on the stalk

explanation.surface: Tiny bananas only four inches long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' might suggest crazy, but here it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses are measured in units of four inches, and a bunch of bananas is called by the same name.

clue.text: What price a horse, Crookback?

blocks.note: surface reading: a buyer asking what a horse costs
setter's reading: Richard III, nicknamed Crookback, offers 'my kingdom for a horse' at Bosworth, so the price is giving up his throne

explanation.surface: Someone haggles with a hunchbacked horse dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Richard III cries 'A horse! A horse! My kingdom for a horse!', so the price of the horse would be renouncing the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrendering a kingdom means a monarch formally giving up the throne, the price Richard offered.

clue.text: Annoyed by record set up - surroundings unhealthy

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means lifted so the letters read from the bottom upwards
the second word forms the surroundings, enclosing the first on both sides

blocks.note: LP is a long-playing record
an unhealthy body is a diseased one

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated by a record player in grimy, sickly surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone displeased is vexed or irritated, so the past participle matches the adjective.

clue.text: Money subsequently invested in fuel provides such security

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go within the next word

blocks.note: coal is a fuel
L is the abbreviation for pound, a unit of money
subsequently means later

explanation.surface: Funds put into a fuel business later serve as a guarantee.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is an asset pledged as a guarantee for a loan, which is the security the clue describes.

clue.text: Chances of firsts in our Donkey Derby sprints

indicators.note: firsts means the opening letters of each of the following words are taken

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Betting on who will win the races at the village donkey derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are probabilities, the likelihood of something happening, so they are chances.

clue.text: Law of Modes and Persians like bells forever silenced?

definitions.text: Law of Modes and Persians like bells forever silenced?

blocks.clueFragment: Law of Modes and Persians like
blocks.note: surface reading: an unchangeable law, as in the biblical 'law of the Medes and Persians'
setter's reading: bells that can never ring out again cannot be rung

explanation.surface: An ancient unchangeable law compared to church bells that will never ring again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modes' is a misprint for Medes: the law of the Medes and Persians, from the Book of Daniel, could never be revoked. A bell's ringing is a peal, hence the pun on 'not able to peal again'.
explanation.definitionFit: A law that cannot be revoked or cancelled is permanent, like the Persian decrees in Daniel.

clue.text: Like my aversion to a type of psalm -lacking balance

indicators.note: read as a-version, a turning away, so the word before it is turned around

blocks.note: like means as
taken as written before being turned
a metrical psalm is one versified in regular metre for singing

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a dislike of a certain style of psalm that seems unbalanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aversion' looks like dislike, but split it is a turning: YM. Metrical psalms are the rhymed versions sung in churches, like the Scottish Psalter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something asymmetrical has unequal sides, so it is out of proportion or uneven.

clue.text: Extremely 'hot to preserve one's lineage

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it
one's descent is one's ancestry

explanation.surface: Someone is passionate about keeping their family line going.
explanation.definitionFit: Candescent means glowing white from intense heat, so it describes something extremely hot.

clue.text: One whose opposite number grows up in a cave

definitions.text: One whose opposite number grows up in a cave

blocks.clueFragment: One whose opposite number grows up
blocks.note: surface reading: a person whose counterpart spent their childhood in a cave
setter's reading: limestone formations in caverns come in pairs, one rising from the floor and one hanging from the roof

explanation.surface: Someone's counterpart was raised in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: The partner that grows upward from the floor is a stalagmite; the answer is its partner, which hangs down from the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral icicle hangs from cave ceilings, matched by a column rising from the floor below.

clue.text: Shooting stars with this in olden days?

definitions.text: Shooting stars with this in olden days?

blocks.note: surface reading: meteors streaking across the sky, or perhaps gunfire
setter's reading: navigators 'shot' a star by measuring its altitude with an early instrument

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what people used for meteors in times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting stars' suggests meteors, but to shoot a star is navigators' jargon for measuring its height above the horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: Before the sextant, sailors and astronomers measured the altitude of heavenly bodies with this disc-shaped instrument.

clue.text: Craftsman is one among the craftier sort

indicators.note: among means placed in the midst of the following letters
to sort things is to rearrange them into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; 'the' only reads naturally
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A skilled workman counts among the more cunning types.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled mechanic or maker of things, a craftsman by trade.

clue.text: No 19, his - something more

definitions.note: describes an actor; the answer names the actor

blocks.note: first meaning: 19 is TITLE ROLE, and a film ... is the one who certainly does not have it
second meaning: an additional item, an addition beyond the usual

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 19 across: an actor whose part is no title role but a non-speaking crowd part.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit-part player in a crowd scene, and also anything additional or supplementary, share this word.

clue.text: Nimble-fingered student enters Chinatown

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: deft means nimble and skilful with the hands
L is a learner, as on a British learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A light-fingered student slips into Chinatown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinatown' wants to be an Asian quarter; read it as china town, the Dutch home of the blue-and-white pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft in the Netherlands is famous for its glazed earthenware, so it is a town of china.

clue.text: Part of· the play so called

definitions.text: Part of· the play so called

blocks.note: surface reading: a section of a drama
setter's reading: the part whose character name the play itself bears, as Hamlet in Hamlet

explanation.surface: A section of a play, as it is known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' suggests a scene or act, but it is an actor's part: the character the play is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: The character after whom a play is named, like Macbeth or Hamlet, plays this lead part.

clue.text: Support swindle by one playing . follow-my-leader?

blocks.note: to second a motion is to support it
a fiddle is a cheat or scam

explanation.surface: Someone backs a scam run by a person in a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: Follow-my-leader is a children's game where everyone copies the one in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a subordinate part to someone else, always following their lead, is the idiom for a junior role.

clue.text: Distributes 6s in transactions

blocks.note: first meaning: 6 across is HAND, and a card dealer hands out hands
second meaning: business agreements or bargains

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference turns the first half into handing out cards at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A card dealer passes cards round the table, and business agreements are also called by the same plural noun.

clue.text: Love to wear a hat on the beach-

indicators.note: in a down clue, a hat sits on top, so the covering word is placed above

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is told to put on a sunhat at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public bathing beach or open-air pool, after the Lido in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venice Lido is a famous bathing beach, and the name now covers any public bathing spot.

clue.text: Subjects for 25 in, say, general service

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, as does say
GS is the abbreviation for general service

explanation.surface: Topics for an army scramble in general service.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 across is SCRAMBLING, and these are what gets scrambled at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast cooks whisk and stir these in a pan, so they are the things that get scrambled.

clue.text: Issue shows the enemy driven back

indicators.note: an enemy driven back retreats, so its letters are read from the end

blocks.note: time is 'the enemy', from the stock phrase about time running out

explanation.surface: A military bulletin announces that the enemy has been pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is a familiar crossword name for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give off, which is the verb sense of issue.

clue.text: Communication security procedure when taking off

blocks.note: first meaning: making a signal unintelligible to eavesdroppers
second meaning: fighter aircraft launched in a hurry to intercept an attack

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are military: coding radio traffic, and getting fighters airborne in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Encoding a telephone or radio signal, and hurried take-off of interceptor aircraft, share one word.

clue.text: A very, outlandish-sounding card, this

indicators.note: sounding means we hear the word, and outlandish means in a foreign tongue

blocks.note: très is French for very, pronounced like tray

explanation.surface: Someone describes a playing card as really exotic.
explanation.walkthrough: A trey is the three in a pack of cards or on a die.
explanation.definitionFit: A trey is the playing card bearing three pips, an old name used in card games.

clue.text: Successful, bringing the Duke of Milan to America

indicators.note: bringing one thing to another sets them side by side, one following on

blocks.note: Prospero, the magician of The Tempest, is the deposed Duke of Milan
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An Italian nobleman makes a fortune by emigrating to the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosperous person is thriving and well off, so the adjective means doing well.
